messages:
Aisha (Support): ping — AcmeCorp reporting repeated 429s for dedicated tenant this morning, started ~17:00 UTC. They say requests are being routed to shared-burst and getting throttled. Error snippet from their app: 

AcmeCorp SRE: "response: 429 Too Many Requests (pool=shared-burst)"

Aisha (Support): attaching their sample request headers and a short repro they shared. They claim they have Reserved capacity (acme-dedicated) and were guaranteed capacity.

AcmeCorp SRE: repro curl we used: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \n     -H "x-redwood-tenant: acme" \n     -H "x-redwood-tier: gold, premium" \n     https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

Aisha (Support): note: header has comma-separated tiers (we asked for exact header they sent). They see the response headers: `x-redwood-pool: shared-burst`, `x-rate-limit-reason: capacity`

oncall-bot: incident created #INC-2026-482 (severity: high) — assigned to infra oncall

Ben (Infra): looking. I can see increased 429s from gateway logs for tenant=acme at 17:01:02 UTC and a control-plane routing decision fallback around the same time. Pulling the routing eval trace now.

Ryan (Eng): quick theory — control plane policy parser treats multiple tiers as an array but our fallback matcher expects a single-value string, so when header contains a CSV it fails to match the tenant-specific rule and falls back to default pool. That would route to shared-burst.

Ben (Infra): confirmed in control-plane logs: `route_eval: tiers_parsed=["gold"," premium"] matched_rule=null fallback_pool=shared-burst`. Looks like we trim whitespace differently between runtime and policy store.

Ingrid (SRE): impact: autoscaler for acme-dedicated didn't spin new nodes because control-plane never selected that pool. From node logs: `autoscaler: no_pool_selected for tenant=acme` then cluster saw sudden spike and shared-burst got overloaded. Throttling started ~17:00:50 and peaked 17:02:10.

Aisha (Support): Acme asking for ETA and an immediate workaround — they can't pause traffic.

Ben (Infra): short mitigation: add a tenant override in routing DB to pin `acme -> acme-dedicated` (bypass tier parser). I can push a hotfix rule in ~10m. Long-term fix: normalize CSV tier parsing to trim spaces and match policy keys.

Ryan (Eng): repro script I used locally: 
```
# reproducer
echo -e "GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.example\r\nAuthorization: Bearer deadbeef\r\nX-Redwood-Tenant: acme\r\nX-Redwood-Tier: gold, premium\r\n\r\n" | nc api-gateway 80
```
Produces log: `route_decision: pool=shared-burst reason=tier_parse_error`

Ben (Infra): pushing tenant override now. Will monitor metrics and tracer. Rolling to prod in 2 steps: 1) rule push (immediate), 2) parser patch (tomorrow sprint).

Ingrid (SRE): please also check for other tenants sending CSV tiers (we might have broader hit). I ran a quick query: 12 tenants used comma in tier header last 24h, 3 with reserved pools.

Aisha (Support): letting AcmeCorp SRE know workaround and that we're deploying a hotfix.

AcmeCorp SRE: thanks. We'll enable client-side header normalization for now as an extra precaution. Please keep us posted and cc our account manager.

Ben (Infra): hotfix rule pushed at 17:06:25 UTC — tracer shows subsequent requests for acme now hitting acme-dedicated and 429s dropping. Continue monitoring.

oncall-bot: annotation added to incident #INC-2026-482: remediation=tenant-override applied

Aisha (Support): follow-ups: file a postmortem, list tenants affected, and include recommended header validation in SDKs. Assigning to @Ryan (Eng) for the parser PR and @Ben (Infra) for rollout notes.

Ryan (Eng): will open PR with CSV trimming + unit tests and a canary rollout plan. ETA for PR: EOD today.

Ingrid (SRE): monitoring shows steady recovery, shared-burst CPU normalized. Sending summary to incident channel now.

Aisha (Support): closing loop with Acme. Ticket: SUP-3241, Incident: INC-2026-482.

AcmeCorp SRE: appreciate the fast response :thumbsup:
